apps.name: Base
apps.subtitle: Talk to your agents from iPhone and iPad.
apps.localizedDescription: Base is the native Riad client for following sessions, dictating prompts, and sending messages to your agents.

versions.localizedDescription: Shows an honest disconnected widget state: neutral gray status geometry, normal segmented meters, and em-dash chat rows with no fake names, ages, or stale cached sessions.
Adds more breathing room above recent widget chats, dates recency from completed replies instead of in-flight activity, and removes the meaningless Apple badge from Codex headers.
Adds a little breathing room above recent chats in the Base Status widget, renders complete OMP math during long tool turns, and clears finished OMP todo strips as soon as the live plan disappears.
Centers the small status widget, simplifies recent-chat ages to minutes, and restores SideStore-visible updates with a stable source identifier and marketing-version guard.
Declutters the iPadOS status widget: removes the Base and Recent Chats headings, refresh timer, chat bullets, and horizontal separators; GPU dots now stack above token pressure.
Remote-first iOS dictation with automatic on-device fallback, accurate cross-device chat working status after completed turns, and the latest rendering, widget, window, and efficiency repairs.
Landscape on iPad is fixed: the app now declares every orientation, so iPadOS renders it full-width instead of letterboxing a portrait canvas between black bars.

Sidebar can now be hidden on iPad (toggle in the chat header), a new Row spacing setting (Tight/Default/Roomy) on all platforms, and hosts you have never reached now show their names instead of raw IPs - daemons advertise fleet labels.
iPad now gets a real iPadOS layout: a persistent session sidebar beside the open chat, Mac-style, instead of a stretched phone stack. Includes the week's efficiency and rendering work.

Chats now render only their newest ~20k characters of scrollback instead of laying out megabytes of markdown per update — fat sessions stop feeling sluggish on both platforms. Older history stays on the daemon exactly as before.

Wide markdown tables now stack into labeled per-row cards when the pane is too narrow for every column, instead of hiding most columns behind an unmarked sideways scroll — a 13-column training table is fully readable on the phone.
More space between the GPU dots and the account usage rail in the phone's compact status row.

Major efficiency pass for busy fleets: the phone renders status at a glanceable cadence instead of once per agent event, session rows re-render only when their content changes, transcript cache writes stop comparing every cached conversation, and prefetching parks when the cache is full instead of refetching forever.
Widens the gap between the GPU dots and the account usage rail in the compact status row on iOS and in the macOS hidden-sidebar chat header.

Base now checks for updates every time it opens, so new releases surface immediately instead of waiting out the six-hour cadence. Update capture also reports exactly why it declines and no longer refuses when windows are deferred to other desktops or lack a resolvable display.

Fixes the distorted flash when switching into a chat window and cuts power draw: chats stay mounted across Space and app switches, transcripts pin to the newest message without re-layout jumps, and bursty agent updates coalesce on macOS and iOS instead of re-rendering per event.
Fixes multi-window slowdown: off-Space chats release transcript rendering and polling, visible windows coalesce shared updates, and active chats stay live.
Adds a top-bar jump-to-latest control on macOS and iOS, replaces Stop while reading scrollback, and enables the iOS Send button immediately for prompt answers.

Restores the macOS copy-confirmation checkmark and shows complete normal transcript responses instead of ellipsis previews on macOS and iOS. Also hardens transactional macOS relaunches so staged updates reopen reliably without losing deferred windows.

Improved on-device dictation with a higher-accuracy iPhone default, deterministic decoding, final-word capture, environmental-noise cleanup, and safe lone-word suppression. Also includes hardened Markdown/LaTeX rendering, clearer status rails, per-window macOS compact sidebars, reliable window restoration, and remembered names for disconnected devices.

privacy.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Base records audio for dictation and transcribes it on your Mac Mini when available or on this device.
